items.title: 56800_John Simmons oral history interview
items.q: I used to give Art Tatum a fit, 'cause every time I'd pick up a bass, and he was playing, he'd get up

ctx.x: broke. Left me playing with three strings. And this excited Roy. Oh, he just started dancing all over the bandstand. Say, "Man, come on and go down ever to my job with me." I say, "Your job?" He say, "Yeah, down at the Three Deuces." And then I almost fainted.

So I went down there, and as I said, I used to give Art Tatum a fit, 'cause every time I'd pick up a bass, and he was playing, he'd get up, without even looking at me, 'cause I was out of tune, everything was wrong.

So Roy said (unintelligible). I went up to the bandstand, took the base. First note, Art got up, he didn't have to look up, he knew who it was. So I stayed around there, and I worked with a wonderful musician, a bandleader, four pieces combo -- Les Wilcox. He could write and arrange individual parts. He could write music like you would write a letter, in long-hand. No score. This is the first time I had ever seen anything like that. He liked me. And they didn't have a bass player. So I'd go over there and sit,…
